gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-moderustic: Moderustic has curves that look traced with a broad nib and left a little unfinished. Moderustic sits under Happy Monkey, whose heavy bowls match its stems like cord, and that tension is the pair's real hook.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-molengo: Happy Monkey draws every line like a ruler-straight bar, gaps wide. Molengo, a contemporary sans, keeps tiny sizes crisp, so give it room to work at small sizes while the heading stays loud.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-momo-trust-sans: Momo Trust Sans has bowls as heavy as its stems and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths. And Happy Monkey, bold and distinctive above it, gives that friendly plain sans a loud neighbor to lean against on a long page.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mona-sans: Happy Monkey's strokes never thin out or thicken anywhere. It earns its keep large and brief, while Mona Sans, a plain sans with openings wide as a door left ajar, handles everything after.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-mooli: Distinctive is the right word for Happy Monkey, with its a stripped of any hairline strokes, sitting over Mooli's round, open letters. Mooli then reads smoothly and clearly, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-murecho: Loud, blunt, and a bit cartoonish up top. Happy Monkey is best when its diagonals match its stems at display size, whereas Murecho, a plain sans with s curves open wide at both ends, is best at quiet, steady text.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-nanum-gothic: Happy Monkey keeps its thickness identical in every direction. Nanum Gothic adds wide channels leading into each counter, and that clash of chunky display and open sans is where this pair is strongest.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-national-park: Bold and distinctive, Happy Monkey sets its ruler-straight lines against National Park's rounded letters, each with a clearly open side. Happy Monkey does the shouting; National Park, a pen that never shifts pressure or angle, does the talking.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-niramit: Bold, with one fixed nib width throughout. Happy Monkey is built for making a statement, while Niramit, a sans with gaping letter curves, is built for steady, professional reading.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-noto-sans-canadia: Distinctive neon-tube consistency runs through every Happy Monkey stroke. Noto Sans Canadian Aboriginal, a sans-serif open at every curve end, would carry a longer passage smoothly beneath it.
